summary: LLM inference costs are driven primarily by token consumption (input + output), and unoptimized production apps routinely overspend by 60-90% through redundant context, oversized models, and uncached repeated calls. By combining prompt caching, semantic caching, model cascading, and prompt compression, teams commonly cut API spend by 70-90% (e.g. from $10K to $2K/month) while also improving latency. The highest-leverage move is prompt caching, which can reduce input costs by up to 90% with minimal engineering risk.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuses previously processed static portions of a prompt (system instructions, few-shot examples, document context) so the provider charges a steeply discounted rate for cached input tokens instead of reprocessing them each call.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on repeated input tokens
techniques.example: Place your large unchanging system prompt and RAG context at the start of the message and mark it with Anthropic's cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'} so subsequent requests reuse the cached prefix at ~10% of the input cost.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches LLM responses keyed by the semantic meaning (embedding similarity) of the query rather than exact string match, so paraphrased-but-equivalent questions return a stored answer without hitting the model.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming queries and, if cosine similarity to a cached query exceeds 0.95, serve the stored completion instead of calling the API.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, escalating to a larger, more expensive model only when a cheap model's confidence or output quality is insufficient.
techniques.example: Send all queries to GPT-4o-mini first and only fall back to GPT-4o when a lightweight classifier or a self-grading check flags the cheap model's answer as low confidence.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of tokens in prompts by removing redundancy, trimming boilerplate, summarizing long context, or using compression models like LLMLingua to drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run RAG-retrieved chunks through LLMLingua to compress a 4,000-token context down to ~1,500 tokens before sending it to the model, keeping key facts intact.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting
techniques.description: Constrains response length with max_tokens and explicit formatting instructions, since output tokens are typically 3-5x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=200 and instruct 'Respond in at most 3 bullet points' to prevent the model from generating verbose, costly completions.

techniques.name: Right-Sizing the Model
techniques.description: Selecting the smallest model that meets quality requirements for a given task instead of defaulting to the flagship model for everything.
techniques.example: Switch classification and extraction tasks from GPT-4o to GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash, reserving the premium model only for complex reasoning.

techniques.name: Structured Output & Function Calling
techniques.description: Forcing JSON/schema-constrained outputs eliminates verbose natural-language padding and reduces downstream retry/parse failures that waste tokens.
techniques.example: Use OpenAI's response_format={'type':'json_schema'} so the model returns only the required fields rather than explanatory prose.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Grouping multiple independent tasks into a single call, or using providers' async Batch APIs, to amortize fixed overhead and access discounted batch pricing.
techniques.savings: up to 50% via batch API discounts
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 non-urgent classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get results within 24 hours at 50% off standard pricing.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Streaming responses and stopping generation as soon as the needed content appears (via stop sequences) avoids paying for unnecessary trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define stop=['\n\n'] so generation halts after the first paragraph instead of continuing to the max token limit.

techniques.name: RAG Context Pruning
techniques.description: Retrieving and injecting only the most relevant chunks (via reranking and top-k tuning) rather than stuffing large context windows with marginally relevant text.
techniques.example: Apply a cross-encoder reranker to retrieve 20 candidates but pass only the top 3 highest-scoring chunks to the model.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer that stores LLM responses and serves similar queries from cache using embedding similarity, reducing API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, self-hosted); infra costs only

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Vector-enabled Redis used as a high-performance semantic cache and LLM response store with sub-millisecond lookups.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis OSS free; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/month, enterprise custom

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that routes requests across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, fallback routing, rate limiting, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and proxy platform offering caching, cost tracking, request logging, and rate limiting with a one-line integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/month

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Orchestration framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, GPTCache), model routing, and prompt management abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Framework free; LangSmith observability free tier + paid from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that uses a small model to drop low-information tokens, compressing prompts up to 20x with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, smart model routing, fallbacks, load balancing, and observability across providers.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway for routing across many models/providers with price-based routing and automatic fallbacks.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go per token (small routing fee); no subscription

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching for static system prompts and RAG context to cut input costs by up to 90% with near-zero code changes.
Downgrade non-critical tasks from flagship models to cheaper tiers like GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to serve repeated/paraphrased queries for free.
Set max_tokens and request concise/structured output to stop paying for unneeded, expensive output tokens.
Drop a drop-in proxy like LiteLLM or Helicone in front of your calls to get caching, fallbacks, and cost visibility immediately.
